block shift law: for a word w of length j the section operators send the state (3^j d, 3^{j+i}) to (d + 3^i packWord(w), 3^{j+i}), every such word survives, and at i = 0, j = e the 3^e words of length e reach exactly the states d + t for t in the balanced window W_e = [-(3^e-1)/2, (3^e-1)/2]; the shift is the balanced value packWord(w) and NOT the digit sum, and the distinction is load bearing because W_e is a complete residue system modulo 3^e while the digit sums are only the 2e+1 values |s| <= e

the shifted family separates residues: for every e >= 1 and R >= 0 the map d mod 3^R -> (B_R(d+t))_{t in W_e} is injective, where B_R is the depth-R behaviour of (d+t, 3^e) and W_e is the window of BTL-block-shift; proof by induction on R, using that W_e contains exactly one t_0 with 3^e dividing d + t_0, that t_0 is the unique window entry whose behaviour has depth at least min(e,R) when R > e, and that its entry carries the family of d' = (d+t_0)/3^e at horizon R - e; this closes the 3^{r-e} + e row count for all e, and it is false for the digit-sum window, where d = 3 and d = 6 modulo 9 collide at e = 2

normal form for the minimal deep-regime state: scale by a unit so that b = 3^e with e = min(v_3(b), r); then if v_3(c) < e the depth-r behaviour is the fully ternary tree truncated at depth v_3(c) and depends on v_3(c) alone, giving r classes, while if v_3(c) >= e the behaviour is exactly the unit-scaling orbit of (c, b) modulo 3^r with no further collapse, giving (3^{r+1}-1)/2 classes, and L_r is the sum; so the minimal state is the unit orbit degenerated to v_3(c) where the constant dominates the derivative, which identifies the quotient with classical Newton-polygon dominance plus Hensel rigidity and is why the branch closes as a reparameterization; bijection with behaviour classes verified for r <= 4

for Γ_NP, if E_|v|(s)=E_|v|(t) then T_v(s) lands on F iff T_v(t) does; length-n suffix acceptance is classified by E_n, not by residual coordinates. This is fold_on_F_iff, not a bound on L_0

for F(x)=x^2 and the infinite output language Y={0,+}^ω that never emits -1, the language L of trit words whose residual outputs of F all lie in {0,+} is not regular; equivalently the 3-adic preimage X=F^{-1}(Y) is not sofic. The prefixes 10^m are pairwise Myhill-Nerode inequivalent because the residual g_m(x)=3^{m+1}x^2+2x accepts w_m=(-1)^{m+1}0 while every g_n with n>m rejects it

for F(x)=x^2 write C_F(m,r) for the number of ≡_r classes among the unrestricted residuals of F at input depth m. Then C_F(m,r)=3^m whenever r≥m≥0, and C_F(m,m-1)=3^m-3 for every m≥2. The latter deficit is exactly three doubletons: for each σ in {-1,0,+1}, the two length-m extensions of σ^{m-1} by a trit other than σ are ≡_{m-1}-equivalent, and every other same-depth pair is distinguished

for F(x)=x^2 and r>=1, unrestricted ≡_r types at depth m>r inject into pairs (p mod 3^r, DZ^m(p^2) mod 3^r) for p in P_m. On the fibre p≡0 (mod 3^r): if m=2r the second coordinate runs exactly over the quadratic residues in Z/3^r Z, hence C_{x^2}(2r,r)<3^{2r}; if m>=3r the second coordinate is all of Z/3^r Z, via p=3^r + v 3^{m-r} for v in P_r. This decides the zero fibre, not C_{x^2}(m,r) for a general fibre. Cf. BTR-x2-C-band

for F(x)=x^2, r>=1 and m>=5r, every fibre p≡α (mod 3^r) of the interior map has second coordinate all of Z/3^r Z. Explicitly, for α,u in P_r the prefix p=α + u 3^r + 3^{m-r} lies in P_m, satisfies p≡α (mod 3^r), and DZ^m(p^2)≡2u + DZ^r(2α) (mod 3^r); the unit 2 makes u↦2u+const bijective. In particular no fibre stays incomplete for all m. This is not a first-saturation time of C_{x^2}(m,r). Cf. BTR-x2-C-interior
The LSD carry of normalizing the doubled trit stream 2 d_i, d_i in {-1,0,1}, stays in {-1,0,1}; 1 and -1 are reachable from 0.
V(c)=|c| strictly decreases under c |-> DZ(c+2d) whenever |c|>=2 and d is a trit.
Doubled-trit carry and output are odd: T(-c,-d)=-T(c,d) and the emitted trit negates.
The three carries -1,0,1 have pairwise distinct Mealy output signatures, so the 3-state machine is minimal.
The synthetic map T_3(c,d)=3 DZ(c+2d) satisfies c_n=3n along the all-+1 word, so the residual set is unbounded. This is not value-preserving normalization.
For T(n)=3n-lsd(n), lsd(T(n))=-lsd(n) and lsd(T^k(n))=(-1)^k lsd(n). Future LSD observations depend only on lsd(n).
Laboratory DZ is a left inverse of T: DZ(T(n))=n. Canonical T is the section I_{-lsd(n)}(n), not a constant-section I_a.
T(I_a(x))=9x+2a and lsd(T(I_a(x)))=-a, independent of the higher-digit residual x.
|T(n)| < |n| for all integers n, where T(n)=3n-lsd(n)
For T_λ(n)=3n-λ lsd(n), lsd(T_2(n))=lsd(n) and lsd(T_3(n))=0. The observational residual remains a trit; λ changes the residue map, not the need for the full integer.
For T(n)=3n-lsd(n), the length-2 integer jet satisfies J2(T(n))=(-lsd(n), lsd(n)). The map depends only on the first digit; every trit window (a,b) is sent to (-a,a).
The J2-orbit of T requires lsd(D^2(n)) or otherwise information beyond J2(n)
J2(T_2(n))=(lsd(n),0) and J2(T_3(n))=(0,0). Order-2 observation distinguishes T_2 from T, unlike the one-digit residual.

For T(n)=3n-lsd(n), the length-3 integer jet satisfies J3(T(n))=(-lsd(n), lsd(n), lsd(DZ(n))). Equivalently J3(T(n))=(-a,a,b) when J2(n)=(a,b). The third input digit is discarded. The map factors through J2.
J3(T(n)) is a function of lsd(n) alone
J3(T_2(n))=(lsd(n),0,lsd(DZ(n))) and J3(T_3(n))=(0,0,lsd(DZ(n))). T_3 collapses J1 and J2 but does not collapse J3: the second input digit survives.
D(x+y)=D(x)+D(y)+D(lsd(x)+lsd(y)). The missing state at the unary/Add boundary is D of the local digit sum.
D(x+y) is a function of (D(x), D(y), lsd(x+y))
If s,a,b are trits then D(s+a+b) is a trit. The streaming residual of trit addition is exactly {-1,0,1}. Three values occur on D(x)=D(y)=0, so the residual is minimal.
The shortcut map C(n)=n/2 (even) or (3n+1)/2 (odd) is well-defined on positive integers, and {1,2} is a 2-cycle.
V(n)=n strictly decreases on every shortcut step.
For every L≥1, n=2^L-1 realises L odd shortcut steps and C^L(n)=3^L-1>n. No residual n mod 2^L with blocks of length at most L certifies strict descent.
I_0(x)=3x. If |x|>1 then 3|x| is composite.
I_a(n) mod m depends only on n mod m.
The finite sieve residual gcd(n,210)=1 does not equal Prime: I_0(1)=3 is prime and I_0(211)=633 is composite, with 1≡211 (mod 210).
Equal length-L LSD jets have identical Prime continuation behaviour.
For λ=1 and |u|≤m, if |s|≤⌊m/2⌋ then |D(s+u)|≤⌊m/2⌋. The looser radius ⌈(m+1)/2⌉ from 3|D n|≤|n|+1 is not required.
For F_{λ,U_m}(s,u)=λ·D(s+u) and every integer λ≥0, a finite invariant box containing 0 exists if and only if λ≤2 or m≤1.
Gain λ=3 forces unbounded residual independently of the raw alphabet U.
For F_{2,U_2} the origin-reachable set is {-2,0,2} while the smallest invariant interval is [-2,2]. Interval invariance is not the reachable residual.
r-way trit addition s'=D(s+a_1+⋯+a_r) is F_{1,U_r}: a trit sum of length r has absolute value at most r, so the λ=1 box |s|≤⌊r/2⌋ is invariant. The count 2⌊r/2⌋+1 equals 1,3,3,5 for r=1,2,3,4.

If λ≥3 and |u|≥2 then the constant-control orbit of F_{λ,U} from 0 is unbounded: at λ=3 one has s'=s+u-lsd(s+u) so each step moves by at least 1; at λ≥4 the step is strictly expanding on the matching ray.
For λ=2 and |u|≤m, if |s|≤2 m.pred then |2 D(s+u)|≤2 m.pred. This is the sharp invariant radius 2(m-1)_+.
Holes or asymmetry in the raw alphabet U change the finite/infinite residual phase at fixed (λ, max|u|).
The minimal residual complexity M(λ,U) is determined by (λ, max|u|) alone.
For λ=1 and U_m, every integer s with |s|≤⌊m/2⌋ is reached from 0 by an admissible word. The explicit positive word is u=2,4,...,2n.
For λ=2 and U_m, every even 2n with |n|≤(m-1)_+ is reached from 0 by an admissible word. The explicit nonnegative word uses letters k+2 at step k.
For every finite U, the origin-reachable residual equals λℤ intersect the symmetric invariant interval.
Sign symmetry of U_m forces M(λ,U_m)=|R|/2.

If λ is not divisible by 3 and s≠t, the constant word of any letter of length v_3(s-t)+1 distinguishes the output streams of F_{λ,U}(s,u)=λ·D(s+u) with output lsd(s+u). Distinct residuals are therefore Mealy-inequivalent, so M(λ,U)=|R_{λ,U}| on every nonempty origin-reachable machine in this regime.
At λ=3, translation by 3k preserves every output stream: signedTrace 3 (s+3k) w = signedTrace 3 s w. This symmetry is not origin-reachable when max|u|≤1.
Some listed finite U at λ=1 or λ=2 has M(λ,U)<|R_{λ,U}|.
Identical immediate lsd signatures force behavioral equivalence of residual states.
If λ is not divisible by 3 and s≠t, every word of length v_3(s-t)+1 distinguishes the lsd output streams of F_{λ,U}(s,u)=λ·D(s+u). A common cyclic letter is not required.
3-adic residual rigidity requires a common cyclic or constant legal letter.
Some Model A–D finite control constraint merges distinct residuals at the same control state.
At λ=3, translation by 3k preserves the output stream of every word, so a control-language restriction cannot destroy that symmetry.
If 3^L divides s-t and |w|≤L, then the lsd streams of F_{λ,U} from s and t agree on w. A remaining-horizon L controller therefore merges (s,q_L) and (t,q_L) whenever that congruence holds.
If λ is not divisible by 3, s≠t, and |w|≥v_3(s-t)+1, then the lsd streams differ on w. Finite horizon preserves residual distinguishability exactly when a legal word of that length exists.
Some legal word shorter than v_3(s-t)+1 always separates distinct residuals, even when the control language forbids every critical-length word.
Finite control horizon creates residual merges only through deadlock or empty continuation.

If λ is not divisible by 3 and s≠t, the lsd streams of F_{λ,U} agree on a word w if and only if |w|≤v_3(s-t). A finite control language therefore merges (s,q) and (t,q) exactly when every legal word is shorter than v_3(s-t)+1.
A proper subset of the complete depth-L control tree can merge residuals that some remaining word of length v_3(s-t)+1 would separate.
If F(s,c)=λ·D(s+h(c)) then F(s,(d1,d2))=λ·D(s+d1 d2). Two-trit product residual factors through the raw contribution.
For trit pairs (d1,d2) and any gain λ, λ·D(0+d1 d2)=0. Origin-reachable residual of two-trit product forcing is {0}, matching F_{λ,U_1}.
Three-trit product has a different origin-reachable residual than two-trit product.
The two-trit product machine has a 3-state origin-reachable residual.

For every realized finite Juggler word w, n^{3^{#O(w)}} = T_w(n)^{2^{|w|}} + Δ_w(n), where Δ is the recursively lifted accumulation of local floor remainders. Δ ≥ 0, so the power envelope is a corollary; Δ = 0 iff every local remainder vanishes; concatenation is the two-term power-gap lift, not an additive sum.

For a realized Juggler word w, the first positive local remainder sits after a tight even or odd power-of-two prefix. That remainder contributes at least ρ_j^{2^j} to Δ, and the suffix operator Amplify (later remainders dropped) is a lower bound. An odd letter lifts an inserted defect by the exact cubic (x^a+D)^3-x^{3a} ≥ 3 x^{2a} D. Mixed OOE has firstDefect ≤ 1, with Δ ≥ 3 T(n)^4 ρ_0 or Δ ≥ ρ_1^2. These bounds do not claim Δ exceeds the formal surplus.

For a realized Juggler itinerary, the relative slack 1+q = n^{3^{#O(w)}} / T_w(n)^{2^{|w|}} multiplies under concatenation: 1+q_{uv} = (1+q_u)^{3^{#O(v)}} (1+q_v)^{2^{|u|}}. An even letter multiplies by (1+η)^{2^k}; an odd letter multiplies by (1+q)^3 (1+η)^{2^k}. Running 1+q does not decrease under a realized extension. The surplus ratio R=Δ/S satisfies R≤1 iff T_w(n)≥n whenever S>0, so R is the endpoint comparison in other coordinates. A realized return T_w(n)=n uses the whole formal surplus.

Two consecutive persistent expanding Juggler residual blocks are impossible. Counterexample: 365 follows OOE to 763 and 763 follows OOE to 1749; both steps are PersistentExpandingResidual. An expanding O^a E^b block has a≥2, and a persistent residual endpoint is odd-to-odd so the next residual also has a≥2; that state is compatible with another expanding block. The n≤80 contracting sequels at 37 and 69 are a small-window artifact.

The integer exponent surplus of a finite Juggler word is E(w)=3^{#O(w)}-2^{|w|}, and E(w)>0 if and only if the itinerary is formally expanding. An expanding residual block O^a E^b with b≥1 has b<a. On an expanding itinerary, n^{3^{#O}}=n^{2^{|w|}+E(w)}. Relative slack multiplies under concatenation, and the slack numerator of a three-block word is n^{3^{o(v)+o(w)}}. The chain 365 --OOE--> 763 --OOE--> 1749 --OOE--> 4447 is a PersistentExpansionChain. This does not bound consecutive expanding persistent runs.

For a realized Juggler itinerary, the pair (A,B)=(3^{#O(w)}, 2^{|w|}) multiplies under concatenation, and n^A = T_w(n)^B + Δ_w(n). The 1+q concatenation law is the same identity in multiplier coordinates: 1+q_{uv} = (1+q_u)^{A_v} (1+q_v)^{B_u}. In logarithms this is log T = λ log n - c and the weighted cocycle y_m = Λ_m y_0 - C_m with B_m = C_m/Λ_m. The local comparison c < (λ-1) log n is T_w(n) > n on an expanding itinerary. These are the existing slack identities, not a new obstruction.

Four consecutive persistent expanding Juggler residual blocks exist: 1999 follows OOE to 5169, 5169 follows OOOOEE to 50093, 50093 follows OOE to 193753, and 193753 follows OOE to 887471. Each step is PersistentExpandingResidual.

Positive local slack, after the exact expansion weights, puts a nontrivial upper bound on the density or run length of expanding persistent residual blocks independently of T_w(n)≥n. In particular there is a uniform ε>0 with c/(λ-1)≥ε on every expanding persistent block, or the normalized budget B_m is bounded below independently of the endpoint tautology B_m≤y_0(1-1/Λ_m). Counterexamples: the OOE block at 180370579261640036336071806107777 has 0<q<10^{-30}; B_m/B_taut reaches 10^{-9} on the n≤4000 window; a length-5 all-expanding persistent run starts at 2183.

The local Juggler remainder satisfies 0≤ρ<2T+1, hence η=ρ/T^2 < 2/T + 1/T^2 and 1+η < ((T+1)/T)^2. For the mixed itinerary OOE, 1+q = (1+η0)^3 (1+η1)^2 (1+η2)^4, and 1+q is strictly below the successor-ratio product ((T0+1)/T0)^6 ((T1+1)/T1)^4 ((T2+1)/T2)^8. The same bound at a successor start y depends only on the itinerary of y.

On realized odd-odd OOE starts, the last even remainder dominates the relative slack, and q_OOE(n) has order n^{-9/8}. After 329 follows OOOOOOOOE to y≈1.80·10^{32}, the next OOE block has 0<q<10^{-30} with q/y^{-9/8}≈2.64. Persistent expanding pairs have OOE-sequel q2 tracking y^{-9/8}. Large λ reduces successor q only by inflating y.

If a realized mixed itinerary has q_w(n)→0 then the itinerary converges to an exact rigid monochrome tower. Counterexample: the mixed itinerary OOE at 180370579261640036336071806107777 has 0<q<10^{-30}. Exact equality rigidity has no naive quantitative stability theorem.

A residual-shaped word O^a E^b is formally expanding iff 2^{a+b}<3^a. For a≥1 this is equivalent to a+b ≤ log₂(3^a), or b ≤ maxExpandingEvens(a). In particular a=2 or 3 forces b≤1, and a=4 forces b≤2. This is the syntactic expanding language, not a realized-orbit theorem.

For n≥2, PersistentOddResidual x y if and only if PersistentExpandingResidual x y. A contracting residual cannot overshoot, and 2^k=3^o is impossible for a nonempty residual. The expanding qualifier of a persistent residual is therefore redundant.

The expanding residual word grammar, or a finite residue-mod-8 successor automaton, is an independent obstruction to an infinite persistent expanding chain. Counterexamples: on n≥2 persistence already is expansion, so the attack reduces to T_w(n)>n; the OOE type self-loop 365→763→1749 exits odd-to-even at 4447; every odd class modulo 8 both continues and leaves the PE frontier. A finite run bound M is not proved and is not supplied by this grammar.

T(x)=m if and only if m²≤F(x)<(m+1)², with F(x)=x on the even branch and F(x)=x³ on the odd branch. The landing gap ρ=F(x)-m² satisfies 0≤ρ<2T(x)+1. Odd landing is membership of F(x) in a union of odd-m one-step preimages. These are the existing inverse-floor and remainder-window lemmas under landing names.

The normalized landing position θ=ρ/(2T+1) is a compact state for persistent odd-to-odd continuation: it occupies a proper subinterval of [0,1], or a coarse θ-bin predicts the next landing parity better than a residue class, or θ(T(x)) is a function of θ(x) and the branch. Counterexamples: on odd n≤2000, odd-odd θ occupies [0,0.997] and every tenth of [0,1]; PE-continuation landings span [0,0.995]; next-parity entropy given a θ-bin is ≈0.99, matching x mod 8; θ→θ transitions fill essentially all bins.
If x is odd, T(x)=y is odd, and ρ=x³-y² is the local odd remainder, then ρ is even. This is the opposite parity of peakOddDefect_odd, which requires an even maximum.

On a realized OO word with z=T(T(x)), the sequential defect Γ=x⁹-z⁴ equals globalDefect(x,[odd,odd]). The two-step polynomial (x³-ρ)³=(z²+σ)² is y⁶=y⁶. These are the existing OO slack identity and the local floor identities under sequential names.

The peak slack identity x³=(p^{2^r}+ε)²+δ, which requires an even maximum M, transports to a persistent odd-odd pair. Counterexamples: on every odd-odd start n≤2000, including the residual chain 365, 763, 1749, the landing y=T(x) is odd, so peakOddDefect_odd does not apply and peakOddDefect(x,y) is even.

If y is odd and T(y) is odd, then the local remainder ρ=y³-T(y)² satisfies ρ≡y-1 (mod 8). Consequently v₂(ρ)=1 when y≡3 or 7 (mod 8), v₂(ρ)=2 when y≡5 (mod 8), and v₂(ρ)≥3 when y≡1 (mod 8) and ρ≠0. The same congruences hold for any odd square below y³; the floor T(y)=⌊y^{3/2}⌋ is not used beyond selecting an odd landing.

Persistent-expanding residual history forces a 2-adic landing restriction stronger than y mod 8: either v₂(y³-T(y)²)≥r>1 at a PE endpoint, or y≡1 (mod 16) forces v₂≥4, or the valuation locks the next residual word. Counterexamples: 365 maps to the PE endpoint 763 with v₂=1; 33≡1 (mod 16) has v₂=3; on odd n≤4000 the PE valuation table is the residue law, and v₂=1 continues as both persistent OOE and non-persistent OOEE.

y=T_w(x) with x realising w if and only if follows x w and image x w = y. Each letter is the existing inverse-floor cell: T(n)=m iff m²≤F(n)<(m+1)² with F(n)=n on the even branch and F(n)=n³ on the odd branch. These are the itinerary and cell lemmas under cylinder names.

The predecessor cylinder of a persistent-expanding residual word constrains T(y) mod 2 or the next residual grammar in a way invisible from y, y mod 8, or θ(y). Counterexamples: 3461 maps under OOE to 9585 with T even and 3803 maps under OOE to 10657 with T odd; both endpoints are 1 mod 8 with θ≈0.382. On expanding overshoots n≤4000 every PE word with at least 8 samples realises both next parities.

Write oddLanding y for y odd and T(y) odd, and oddRun 0 y = oddLanding y, oddRun (r+1) y = oddLanding y and oddRun r (T(y)). Then oddRun (r+1) y if and only if y is odd and oddRun r (T(y)). The odd-landing cylinder of a fixed m contains at most one integer.

The iterated odd-landing sets P_r occupy shrinking arithmetic cylinders, or iteration is recognized modulo 2^m, or successive square-gap coordinates on long odd runs are constrained. Counterexamples: on odd n≤8000 the stay fraction |P_{r+1}|/|P_r| is 0.49–0.53 through r=7; P_r is mostly isolated odds; every residue modulo 64 both continues and exits; θ on P_r and on the exit from P_{r-1} both occupy [0,1].

For every natural n and finite parity itinerary w, follows n w if and only if the actual length-|w| Juggler itinerary of n equals w. The itinerary image equals the |w|-fold iterate, and images and realization compose under word concatenation.
If n and m realize the same finite Juggler word w and n ≤ m, then the image of n after w is at most the image of m after w.
For every finite Juggler word w realized at n, J^{|w|}(n)^{2^{|w|}} ≤ n^{3^{#O(w)}}. If n ≥ 2 and 3^{#O(w)} < 2^{|w|}, then J^{|w|}(n) < n.

The even fiber J(n)=m is the parity-restricted square interval m² ≤ n < (m+1)², while the odd fiber is the parity-restricted cube-to-square interval m² ≤ n³ < (m+1)²; any odd fiber contains at most one integer.

Every nontrivial Juggler cycle itinerary based at n ≥ 2 is formally expanding. Cycle extrema satisfy the certified parity, order, square-scale, and nested-cell constraints; a minimum-based cycle orientation cannot end in an odd letter. The path from a cycle minimum to any later even state is superquadratic. These are necessary cycle restrictions, not an exclusion of all cycles.

For S_O(N) = sum over odd n ≤ N of (-1)^{floor(n^{3/2})}, the exact fractional-part formulation together with the classical van der Corput and Erdős–Turán inequalities gives |S_O(N)| ≪ N^{5/6}. This is an ambient odd-input bound, not a Juggler-orbit transfer theorem.

The odd-to-odd Juggler starts have natural density 1/4. Equivalently, the starts that admit a uniform one- or two-step FiniteProgress certificate (every even start n ≥ 2, and every odd start whose first image is even) have natural density 3/4. This is the counting corollary |OO(N)-N/4| ≪ N^{5/6} of the ambient odd-input discrepancy bound. It is a density of that uniform short-certificate class, not of all FiniteProgress, not of ReachesOne, and not a Lean counting theorem.

Universal FiniteProgress for starts above one implies universal reachability of one. Every even start n ≥ 2 and every odd start n ≥ 2 whose first image is even has FiniteProgress; consequently, any start without FiniteProgress is odd and has an odd first image. This isolates the automatic odd-to-odd frontier without proving universal progress.

Neither OOOEOE nor OOOOEE is a Juggler cycle itinerary at any n ≥ 2 (Paper A Lemma 3.5). The argument is an exhaustive evaluation for n < 256 together with the last-even one-step preimage against the coarse lower envelope n^{81} > 2^{130}(n+1)^{64} for n ≥ 256. This excludes those two orientations only; the length-≤6 census is the separate row J-small-cycle-census.

No itinerary of length at most six is a Juggler cycle itinerary at any n ≥ 2; equivalently a nontrivial Juggler cycle, if one exists, has period at least seven (Paper A Theorem 3.6). Assembly: rotation invariance of cycle itineraries, exclusion of all-odd itineraries by strict odd ascent, rotation to an even-terminating orientation, the formal-expansion filter, the next-square thresholds of Lemma 3.4, the leftover exclusions of OOOEOE and OOOOEE (Lemma 3.5; rotation targets of OEOOOE and EOOOOE). Lean theorem no_cycle_itinerary_length_le_six. Strengthened by J-small-cycle-census-seven; this row is the length-≤6 statement only. This is not an exclusion of all cycles and not a halt theorem.

Neither OOOOEOE nor OOOOOEE is a Juggler cycle itinerary at any n ≥ 2 (Paper A Lemma 3.7). The argument is an exhaustive evaluation for n < 14 together with the last-even one-step preimage against the coarse lower envelope n^{243} > 2^{422}(n+1)^{128} for n ≥ 14. This excludes those two orientations only; the length-≤7 census is the separate row J-small-cycle-census-seven.

No itinerary of length at most seven is a Juggler cycle itinerary at any n ≥ 2; equivalently a nontrivial Juggler cycle, if one exists, has period at least eight (Paper A Theorem 3.8). Assembly: the length-≤6 census, the formal-expansion filter on length seven, the odd-run exclusion of O^6E, the internal-E bootstrap exclusions of OOEOOOE and OOOEOOE, rotation of EOOOOOE and OEOOOOE onto the leftovers, and the leftover exclusions of OOOOEOE and OOOOOEE (Lemma 3.7). Lean theorem no_cycle_itinerary_length_le_seven. Strengthened by Paper A Theorem 3.22 / Corollary 3.23 (even-count at most three is impossible, so the period is at least eleven). This is not an exclusion of all cycles and not a halt theorem.

No itinerary of length at most eight is a Juggler cycle itinerary at any n ≥ 2; equivalently a nontrivial Juggler cycle, if one exists, has period at least nine. Assembly: the length-≤7 census, the formal-expansion filter on length eight, the odd-run exclusion of O^7E, Theorem 3.12 at k=8, rotation of EOOOOOOE and OEOOOOOE onto those leftovers, and the internal-E bootstrap exclusions of OOOOEOOE, OOOEOOOE, and OOEOOOOE. Lean theorem no_cycle_itinerary_length_le_eight in LengthEightCensus.lean. Implied by Paper A Corollary 3.23 (period at least eleven). Strengthened by J-small-cycle-census-ten. This is not a length-9 itinerary census and not a halt theorem.

If a Juggler cycle itinerary based at n ends with r ≥ 1 even letters, the state immediately before that trailing even run is strictly less than (n+1)^{2^r}. The case r = 1 is the last-even one-step preimage; r = 2 is the two-even bound of Paper A Lemma 3.5 on OOOOEE; r = 3 is the three-even bound for OOOOOOEEE. Lean theorem cycle_trailing_evens_lt. This is a one-step-preimage identity, not a leftover exclusion and not a halt theorem.

OOOOOOEEE is not a Juggler cycle itinerary at any n ≥ 2. The argument is an exhaustive evaluation for n < 128 together with the three-even cell z < (n+1)^8 against the coarse lower envelope n^{729} > 2^{1330}(n+1)^{512} for n ≥ 128. The computational prefix-cell first fires at N0 = 73; 128 is the algebraic cutoff. This excludes that one three-even leftover only; it is not a length-9 census, not an exclusion of the remaining eight leftovers, and not a halt theorem. Lean theorem no_cycle_itinerary_ooooooeee.

For every k ≥ 6 and every n ≥ 2, the even-terminating two-even leftover O^{k-2}EE is not a Juggler cycle itinerary. Large n uses the shared tail n^{3^{k-2}} > 2^{e_{k-2}}(n+1)^{2^k} at the uniform algebraic cutoff n ≥ 256, obtained by cubing the length-6 comparison; e_a = 2(3^a-2^a) = log2(lowerDenom(O^a)). For odd n ≥ 3 with m = floor(n^{3/2}): m^{3/2} = (3/2) m n^{3/4} - (1/2) n^{9/4} + E(n) with 0 ≤ E(n) ≤ (3/8)(n^{3/2}-1)^{-1/2} ≤ (1/2) n^{-3/4}. Companion gap lemma: m(n+2h) - m(n) = floor(delta) + [ {n^{3/2}} ≥ 1 - {delta} ] with delta = (n+2h)^{3/2} - n^{3/2}, giving constant-gap cells of length about n^{1/2}/h. Both validated by exact scaled-integer arithmetic through n = 10^{12}.

Imported into the parity-discrepancy paper as Theorem 4.4. Lean covers only the exact floor reductions (floor_gap_eq_carry gap cells, floor_odd_iff_half_le_fract_half parity bridge); the analytic estimate is a human proof.

Validated by exact scaled-integer arithmetic through n = 10^{12}, worst ratio 0.9970 against supremum 1.

Validated by exact scaled-integer arithmetic (scale 10^{60}) through n = 10^{12}. The tier-2 discrepancy bound was subsequently proved (row J-kernel-cancellation, Theorem R).

Conditional implication (Proposition J): if for every itinerary word w of length d the class count satisfies |#w(N) - 2^{-d} N| ≤ E_d(N), then the starts with no contracting prefix of length ≤ d number at most (N_d/2^d) N + N_d E_d(N), where N_d counts the length-d words with no contracting prefix. That count is exact: 3^{o_t} ≥ 2^t must hold at every t ≤ d and depends on nothing but (t, o_t), so N_d is a dynamic program over the triangle 0 ≤ o ≤ t ≤ d, in integers. The closed form N_d ≤ 2^d e^{-cd} with c = 2 (log2/log3 - 1/2)^2 > 0.0342 follows by dropping every constraint but t = d and applying Hoeffding to the odd-letter count (o_d ≥ d log2/log3); that closed form is what this row carried until 2026-09-05, and it is lossy by 6.7 at d = 5, 43.6 at d = 40 and 1.3e4 at d = 1600. The loss is not in the rate -- the sharp value is -log rho = 0.034688 against Hoeffding's 0.034285, one part in eighty -- but polynomial: N_d/2^d ~ C rho^d d^{-3/2} with C about 11, the d^{-1/2} for staying nonnegative under the zero-drift tilt and a further d^{-1} because the tilted endpoint sits at height ~sqrt(d) rather than at the origin. Every other start n ≥ 2 has a uniform power-envelope descent certificate within d steps (row J-power-envelope-contraction). Hence all-depth parity equidistribution with power savings (Conjecture K; proved unconditionally for all itineraries of length ≤ 4 — rows J-triple-parity-discrepancy, J-even-branch-third-letter, J-depth4-slow-branch, J-depth4-complete; depth ≥ 5 open) implies that the set of Juggler starts admitting a finite descent certificate has natural density one — the Juggler analogue of the Terras program. E-rooted words have a contracting prefix at length 1, so only O-rooted class bounds are ever consumed. The implication is unconditional; the hypothesis is open beyond the proved cases. Not a termination claim; no unconditional density-one claim. Imported into the finite-dynamics note as Proposition 6.1. The exact count at d = 5 has four survivors -- OOOOO, OOOOE, OOOEO, OOEOO -- hence certificate density 1 - 4/32 = 7/8, which is Paper B Corollary 6.4's figure reached by counting words rather than contractors; d = 6 is 7/8 again, since all eight children survive.

(B) Full equidistribution is not needed: if for each fixed depth every surviving class sends O-share at most 1 - beta with beta > beta* = 1 - log2/log3 = 0.36907..., rate-free, then the never-contracting measure at depth d is <= exp(-D(gamma || 1-beta) d) by generating-function domination (sum over classes of mu(sigma) x^{o(sigma)} <= (beta + (1-beta)x)^d) and Chernoff at gamma = log2/log3 (a never-contracting itinerary has o_d >= gamma d), and density one follows the same way. The Heisenberg lift does not transfer Proposition 7.4 (J-shift-average-square-root) from almost every shift to lambda = 0. Proposition JJ survives in this language: (i) integration over lambda is Haar on the center and pinning the identity section is the same specific-point problem (no new second averaging variable; named family averages stay forbidden); (ii) a Fourier mode j of the vertical coordinate is the orbit at amplitude j A (inverse self-similarity); (iii) y-translation deposits -A lambda in the center, so S_lambda decorrelates at scale 1/A_max ~ P^{-27/16} (the same scale). Probe witnesses (exact Fractions; scaled-integer gap 0; 24 horizontal forms, min torus distance 0.0023, max spread 0.46; cheap typicality at P = 10^6: |S_0|/sqrt(L) mean 0.946 vs grid 0.888, median rank 17/32 — typicality is not a transfer). Not a K3 bound, not a proof of HH, not a halt theorem; Paper B frozen.

Validated to n = 10^{12} (smoothing) and n ≤ 20001 (indicator identity). Imported into the parity-discrepancy paper as Proposition 4.5.

Theorem Q: #OEOE(N), #OEOO(N) = N/16 + O(N^{7/8+eps}) and #OEEE(N), #OEEO(N) = N/16 + O(N^{13/16+eps}). No differencing and no kernel: the coefficient crosses integers every P^{5/8}/k steps, unlike the OOO* weight (crossings within single steps) — the engine reaches exactly the letters whose phase coefficients grow slower than n. Ambient counting; not a termination claim; OOO* remains open (Conjecture O). Imported into the finite-dynamics note as Theorem 5.8.

This is an exact identity, not a kernel bound, and does not produce runs on which J is frozen (row J-increment-first-K3). Validated by exact scaled-integer arithmetic through n = 10^{12}.

The OOOO* kernel K3 is bounded by differencing the phase c θ₃ first on X-cell b-runs of floor(ΔX) and then increment-linearizing Z = v^{3/2} along a frozen J = floor(ΔY) (Lemma Z1 leftover α = 29/16, then Theorem R). False: (i) those b-runs do not freeze J — floor(ΔY), Δv, and the κ-fixed branch increment floor((m+b+κ)^{3/2}-m^{3/2}) all have mean and max run length 1 at P = 10^4, 10^5, 10^6, while the b-runs themselves have length ≍ P^{1/2}; the raw increment jumps by ≍ P^{3/4} (level-1 carry flicker) and the branched increment still changes by ≍ P^{1/4} ≫ 1 per step; (ii) changing J by 1 reintroduces the W-family at α = 45/16 via ∂F_J/∂J = (3/2)(v+J)^{1/2}, since c · ∂F_J/∂J / ((9/8) n^{45/16}) → 1 (the Phase-12 wall of row J-scale-invariant-R-extension). Replacing frozen J by J = ΔY - {ΔY} + κ expands a full-size sawtooth of the slow form ΔY, a recorded Phase-5 dead route. Conjecture V (that K3 itself cancels) is not refuted. Not a termination claim.

Lemma Z3: the X1 substitution C{F} = C F - C floor(F) produces a usable frozen-gap integer I = floor(F) if and only if floor(ΔF) is constant on long runs, which for unit steps requires F'' < 1. Instances: F = v^{1/2} (F'' ≍ n^{-7/8} < 1) and F = m^{1/2} (F'' ≍ n^{-5/4} < 1) freeze on a window of 400 odd steps at P = 10^4, 10^5, 10^6; F = Y = m^{3/2} (Y'' ≍ n^{1/4} > 1) has mean and max run length 1 (row J-scale-invariant-R-extension). This is the reason Lemma X1 could land on w and the reason the same move cannot land on v. Not a kernel bound.

The OOOO* leftover C θ₂ with C ≍ n^{45/16} (row J-level3-inner-linearization) is absorbed by an X1 substitution into an integer whose first gap freezes, leaving only engine sawtooths. False: X1 lands on I = floor(Y) = v (Lemma Z3), and Y'' ≍ n^{1/4} > 1 so v has no J-runs. For every tested hybrid Q = v - P with P a polynomial in the freezing integers {w_m^3, m w_m, w^2}, ΔQ has mean and max run length 1 at P = 10^4, 10^5, 10^6. Cubing the T1 expansion of z^{1/2} after absorbing the first-letter θ produces a remainder 3 n^{27/8} m^{-3/8} θ₂ ≍ 3 n^{45/16} θ₂, the same leftover. Conjecture V is not refuted. Not a termination claim.

The nested-floor fifth-letter sum differs from the smooth model e(α n^{81/16}) (or e(α m^{27/8}), or e(α v^{9/4})) by an absorbable error, so K3 can be bounded without forming a W-family. False: Lemma V2 says the pointwise phase defect Y^{3/2} - v^{3/2} is (3/2) m^{3/4} θ₂ + E₂, and restoring the outer coefficient produces the W-family at α = 45/16; Lemma V1 says the outer defect v^{9/4} - z^{3/2} is the K3 phase itself. The error sum is the obstruction, not a remainder. A comparison to the smooth van der Corput sum is therefore circular. Conjecture V is not refuted.

Proposition BB: every method in the laboratory toolkit for K3 dies by one of two mechanisms. (I) It needs a frozen first difference of Y = m^{3/2} (copy of R one nesting up; increment-first on X-cells; X1 landing on v or a v-hybrid). Those cells do not exist (Y'' ≍ n^{1/4} > 1; rows J-scale-invariant-R-extension, J-increment-first-K3, J-x1-absorption-K3). (II) It produces a W-family e(C θ₂) with C ≍ n^{45/16} (V2 then invoke R; replace nested floors by smooth powers). This α exceeds Theorem R's engine line 9/4, the spawned Step-3 coefficient is ≍ n^{25/16} > n, and the amplitude itself satisfies C(n+2)-C(n) ~ (405/64) n^{29/16} >> 1, so R's quasi-static windows cannot run even if the engine line moved toward 2. Therefore the toolkit cannot bound K3. Conjecture V (that K3 cancels) is not refuted. Not a termination claim.

Proposition CC: no family-averaging method (double large sieve, dispersion, amplification over the mode index k) can by itself bound the depth-5 class count. Every Fourier expansion of the parity places weight ≍ 1/k on the k-th harmonic, so the count needs |K3(k)| = o(N) for each bounded k — the k = 1 term carries weight one — while dispersion controls only k-averages, which do not constrain any individual bounded-k coefficient; the phase u(n) admits no auxiliary amplification family; and the Selberg-majorant route to the pair-count obligation expands into the kernel family itself (circular). The Phase-17 spacing statistics stand as OBSERVATION. Refutes the dispersion route as a completion method, not any equidistribution statement.

Lemma DD: on blocks of L = P^{1/4} consecutive odd steps starting at n0, (i) m(n0+2t) = floor(X0 + D t) + O(1) with X0 = n0^{3/2}, D the first X-increment (quadratic drift ≤ 3/2, so defect ≤ 2); (ii) with mu(t) = m0 + A t (A the realized first m-gap) and s(t) = m(t) - mu(t) — a circle-rotation carry sequence floor({X0} + gamma t) + O(1), gamma = D - A — one has v(n0+2t) = floor(mu(t)^{3/2} + (3/2) mu(t)^{1/2} s(t)) + O(1) (Taylor remainder ≍ P^{-1/4}). On P^{1/4}-blocks the nested level-2 data collapses to a bounded-complexity system: smooth affine base plus one rotation orbit amplified by W ≍ P^{3/4}, with block parameters distributed by proven level-≤2 statistics. Substrate of Conjecture EE (the transport inductive step); measured defects ≤ 2 and ≤ 1 at P = 10^4..10^10. Not a K3 bound; Conjectures V and EE stay open.

Lemma FF: on DD-blocks, with F = mu^{3/2} + (3/2) mu^{1/2} s, v = floor(F) + d, e = d - {F}: theta_3 = { mu^{9/4} + (9/4) mu^{5/4} s + (27/32) mu^{1/4} s^2 - (27/128) mu^{-3/4} s^3 + (243/2048) mu^{-7/4} s^4 + ((3/2) mu^{3/4} + (9/8) mu^{-1/4} s - (27/64) mu^{-5/4} s^2) e + (3/8) mu^{-3/4} e^2 } + O(P^{-19/16}), and (3/4) z^{1/2} = (3/4)(mu^{9/8} + (9/8) mu^{1/8} s - (27/128) mu^{-7/8} s^2) + (9/16) F^{-1/4} e + O(P^{-13/16}), modelling the kernel phase u = (3/4) z^{1/2} theta_3 mod 1 to ~P^{-15/16}. The product form multiplies theta_3 model error by z^{1/2} ≍ P^{27/16}, so the expansion must run three orders past sub-unit — the precision budget of the transport cascade. Validated in exact integers at scale 10^48: theta_3 error 5e-11 (P=10^4) down to 4e-25 (P=10^10); u error 2e-4 down to 2e-8. Discharges obligation (γ) of Conjecture EE: the level-3 kernel phase on a block is an explicit closed form in (mu, s, d, {F}); no nesting remains to be modelled. Not a K3 bound; Conjectures V and EE stay open.

Proposition GG: no intra-block harmonic method in the laboratory toolkit bounds the kernel block sums sum_{t<L} e(k C {Theta}) (C ≍ P^{27/16}, Theta the Lemma-FF phase), at any block length L ≤ P. (I) Window drift: any character expansion in the Theta-direction has its Fourier window centered at kC(t), which drifts by kC' ≍ k P^{11/16} per step, so inner sums at fixed harmonic have length < 1 — vacuous, and independent of block length since the drift is per-step in n. (II) Amplitude transfer: floor-splitting e(k floor(C){Theta}) = e(k floor(C) Theta) is exact but its residual double-Fourier collapses back onto the moving-integer phase; the exact identity C theta_3 = (3/4)(z^{1/2} v^{3/2} - z^{3/2}) converts to pure phases whose floor expansions regenerate the alpha = 45/16 W-family; differencing at any order preserves the full amplitude on theta_3-differences (cross-block variance = the T1-family, dead by Proposition BB); interval-splitting needs R ≥ kC cells and its l^1-mass equals the amplitude. Covers the carry-free case (smooth monomials). Both known proof routes to K3 (global toolkit, Proposition BB; intra-block program, this row) are now closed by named mechanisms. Conjectures V, EE, HH are not refuted. Not a termination claim.

Conjecture HH (the pure amplitude-product model): for smooth monomial-type A(t), B(t) on [0, L] with 1 << A' << A (Juggler instance: A = (3k/4) mu^{9/8}, B = mu^{9/4}, mu affine, A ≍ P^{27/16}, A' ≍ P^{11/16}), the sum |sum_{t≤L} e(A(t){B(t)})| ≤ L^{1-delta}. The minimal crystal of the K3 program: all Juggler-specific structure (carries, defects, nesting) stripped. The known boundary is A' ≍ 1: for A' << 1 partial summation makes the amplitude a tame passenger (the engine and the Piatetski-Shapiro literature); for A' >> 1 no tool applies (Proposition GG). Census: R = |S|^2/L has a textbook Exp(1) profile at P = 10^6, 10^8, 10^10, k = 1, 2 (pure_model_census) — square-root cancellation, COMPUTATIONALLY unrefuted, analytically untouched.

Proposition 7.4 of the parity-discrepancy paper (shift-averaged L^2 bound; formerly 'Lemma II' with an overquantified corollary, corrected in Phase 26): let A_1 < ... < A_L be reals with |A_t - A_t'| >= A'_min |t - t'| for some A'_min >= 1 and let x_1, ..., x_L be arbitrary reals. For S_lambda = sum_{t<=L} e(A_t {x_t + lambda}): | int_0^1 |S_lambda|^2 dlambda - L | <= (6/pi)(L/A'_min)(log L + 1), by direct integration (each pair phase is piecewise linear in lambda with real slope A_t - A_t' on at most three arcs). Corrected consequence via Markov: |S_lambda| <= sqrt((L/eps)(1 + (6/pi)(log L + 1)/A'_min)) outside a shift set of measure <= eps — square-root cancellation times sqrt(log L) in general, genuine square-root only when A'_min >> log L (true in the level-3 instance, A'_min ~ P^{11/16}). The former 'in particular |S_lambda| <= sqrt(L/eps) off measure eps(1+o(1))' was false as quantified (the exceptional measure carried an O(log L) factor). The average says nothing about the single shift lambda = 0; it does not make the level-3 kernel 'generically cancelling' in any sense bearing on Conjecture 7.3. Validated by shift_average_probe (mean R = 1.0042 at P = 10^6, 0.9961 at P = 10^8).

Proposition JJ (the de-randomization obstruction): no laboratory tool transfers Lemma II from almost-every shift to lambda = 0. (i) No second averaging variable: amplitude separation forces |A(p) - A(q)| <= 1 to imply p = q, so the only amplitude-frozen lattice direction is trivial; every available family average (block index, integer base mu_0, the k-family) re-enters the T1-family or the amplitude-product class (Propositions BB, GG, CC). (ii) Inverse self-similarity: any concentration/discrepancy inverse for A{B} mod 1 is a statement about sum e(j A {B}) — the same class with amplitude jA; the class is closed under its own inverse theory. (iii) Metric non-transfer: |dS/dlambda| <= 2 pi A_max L, so S_lambda decorrelates at shift scale 1/A_max ≍ P^{-27/16} (measured: increments 0.06-0.08 sqrt(L) at delta = 0.1/(2 pi A), 0.57-0.74 sqrt(L) at 1/(2 pi A), saturated at 10x); almost-all statements leave ~ eps A_max bad cells and cannot pin lambda = 0. HH at lambda = 0 is a specific-point-in-metric-theory problem (the 'is sqrt(2) normal' species); the instance's special arithmetic A^2 = (9/16) k^2 z re-enters the harmonic toolkit via its known exploitations. Third and final layer of the K3 obstruction (after BB, GG); the K3/HH line is PARKED here.

Not a termination claim.

AboveAnchor(n,w) means n follows w and every T^i(n) for i ≤ |w| is at least n. CycleMin(n,w) implies AboveAnchor(n,w). MinimalNonTerm(n) implies AboveAnchor(n,w) for every realized finite prefix w. Among nonnegative exponent walks with a prescribed (L, o) (u_k = (1+μ)a_k − k ≥ 0, μ = log_2(3/2)), the hug itinerary that takes E iff u ≥ 1 and an even remains is the unique prefix-minimal path. First disagreement with any other admissible word is hug-E versus other-O, because hug takes O only when E is illegal and the two words share the same prefix state; the odd-count gap δ_k = a_k(other) − a_k(hug) is a path in {−1,0,+1} that cannot go negative, since δ = 0 restores the same state. Feasible pairs ( (1+μ)o ≥ L ) never strand: o_left = 0 implies u = surplus + e_left ≥ e_left. The charge g(u) = 1/(n^{2^u} 2^u ln n) is strictly decreasing, so hug uniquely maximises the walk sum. This is a statement about the u ≥ 0 relaxation, not about realized cycle itineraries. Not a halt theorem.

The infinite hug walk is rotation by α = log_2(3/2) on the circle R/(1+α)Z. This is the infinite-itinerary average, not a finite-L inequality: leftover hug C exceeds C_* by up to 1.57e-5 on the certified 19-row survey, so C_hug ≤ C_* is false. The Juggler conjecture as an almost-all statement (fate-contagion note, Corollary 4.5). Fix N_0 with [1, N_0] ⊆ R (Lean N_0 = 260, reachesOne_of_lt_two_hundred_sixty_one; certified N_0 = 3.5·10^8). The following are equivalent: (1) every n ≥ 1 reaches 1; (2) Σ_{n ≤ x, n ∉ R} 1/n = o((log x)^λ) for some λ < λ** = 0.448…; (3) the starts n ≤ x whose orbit never enters [1, N_0] have logarithmic count o((log x)^λ) for some λ < λ**. In natural-density terms (3) asks that all but O(x (log x)^{−0.55}) starts below x eventually fall below N_0 — a Tao-type almost-bounded-values statement with a bounded target and a mild logarithmic rate. For Collatz the analogous implication fails because preimage trees are thin (Krasikov–Lagarias x^{0.84}); for the Juggler map the even preimage interval makes fates contagious. This is a reduction, not a proof of termination, and no almost-all statement of type (3) is proved.

Certified closure of the Lean seed [1, 260] under the even-block and OE-fiber productions, computed exactly to 10^9 (research.juggler_sequence.fate_contagion, summary.json): every member reaches 1 (Lean even_block_mem, oe_fiber_mem with reachesOne_backwardClosed). Density 0.45–0.49 on every dyadic block (2^k, 2^{k+1}], 16 ≤ k ≤ 29, against 0.25 for the E-only closure; at x = 10^9 the log-mass on (√x, x] is 3.785 (even) + 1.547 (odd), with realised recursion coefficients 0.9998 (E, theory 1) and 0.3332 (OE against the source mass on (x^{3/8}, x^{3/4}]; heuristic 1/3; proved 1/3 on even blocks and 2/9 elsewhere). Classification FATE_CONTAGION_RECURSION_CONSISTENT. A census of the recursion, not a density theorem.

Odd generation of two-way closed fate classes (fate-contagion note, Theorem 6.1). Fate classes are forward-closed as well as backward-closed (ForwardClosed; reachesOne_forwardClosed, not_reachesOne_forwardClosed, escapes_forwardClosed; mem_iff_floorPower_mem). For a class A that is closed both ways with 1 ∉ A: every member n ≥ 1 descends by even steps only to an odd member of A (exists_odd_ancestor: ∃ k with floorPower^[k] n odd and in A, all earlier iterates even), that member is ≥ 3 (exists_odd_ancestor_ge_three), the odd members are exactly the odd preimages of A ∩ {⌊m^{3/2}⌋ : m odd} (odd_mem_iff: for odd n, A n ↔ A (Nat.sqrt (n^3))), and A is nonempty iff it contains ⌊m^{3/2}⌋ for some odd m ≥ 3 (nonempty_iff_odd_image_mem). Consequence: every positive integer reaches 1 iff no image ⌊m^{3/2}⌋ of an odd m fails to reach 1; the failure set is the E-forest over the odd preimages of F ∩ S. This is the exact skeleton of the S-fairness reformulation: the one free term of the first-letter decomposition (6.1) is the share of OO-type odd numbers whose image lies in F. Not a halt theorem.

Localized triple parity discrepancy and the OOEEE production (fate-contagion note §7). Proposition 7.1: for every ε > 0, P ≥ P₀(ε), every interval I ⊆ (P, 2P] of length Y ≥ P^{1/2}, and every (a,b,c) ≠ 0, |Σ_{n∈I odd} ψ(n^{3/2})^a ψ(m^{3/2})^b ψ(v^{1/2})^c| ≤ Y P^{−1/24+ε} — Paper B's Theorems 4.4/4.7 with the seven proof steps re-run over I: every displayed bound is either proportional to the number of summands (and becomes ∝ Y) or independent of it and ≤ P^{7/16} (two end cells P^{3/8}, pure passenger P^{7/16}, majorant tails P^{1/4}), absorbed for Y ≥ P^{1/2}. Proposition 7.2: for I(m') = [m'^{32/9}, (m'+1)^{32/9}) (length ≍ P^{23/32}), the odd starts with word OOEEE and J^5(n) = m' number (1/16)·#{odd n ∈ I(m')} + O(|I(m')| m'^{−4/27+ε}) (Proposition 7.1 plus a Vaaler layer for ψ(v^{1/4}) → ψ(n^{9/16}) handled by Kusmin–Landau), and every such n has J^4(n) ∈ E(m'); hence for m' in a backward-closed A they lie in A with log-mass ≥ (1/(9m'))(1 − o(1)). Theorem 7.3: the contagion recursion gains (1/9)·g(9t/32) and Theorem 4.2 holds for every λ < λ*** = 0.5392…, the root of 2^{−λ} + (1/9)(3/8)^λ + (2/9)(3/4)^λ + (1/9)(9/32)^λ = 1. Downstream: Tao rate threshold 0.4608, least C = 18 (fair), C(0.55) = 39. The free term ψ_F of (6.1) is untouched; the gain is quantitative. Paper B §4.5 (Theorems 4.11–4.12, Corollary 4.13; J-parity-triple-discrepancy-localized) now proves the localized and twisted statements in full, so this production rests on a Paper B theorem; Paper B remains a working draft.

Paper B §3.5, Lemma 4.10 and Theorems 4.11–4.12 (nested and triple parity discrepancy on sub-dyadic intervals, with a slow twist). For every ε > 0 there is P₀ such that for P ≥ P₀, every interval I ⊆ (P, 2P] of length Y ≥ P^{1/2}, every (a,b,c) ∈ {0,1}³ ∖ {0} and every slow twist g(n) = (ℓ/2) n^{9/16} with |ℓ| ≤ P^{1/24}: |Σ_{n ∈ I odd} ψ(n^{3/2})^a ψ(m^{3/2})^b ψ(v^{1/2})^c e(g(n))| ≤ Y P^{−1/24+ε} (Theorem 4.12; Theorem 4.11 is the case c = 0). Proof: Steps 1–7 of Theorems 4.4/4.7 run over I with the number of summands Y in place of P; every cost is proportional to Y except three absolute terms — the two partial end cells 5.2 (jh)^{−1/2} P^{3/8}, the pure passenger 3.8 P^{7/16}, the majorant end cells 17 P^{1/4} — which fall below Y P^{−1/24} for Y ≥ P^{1/2}; the twist survives the Weyl differencing as e(Δ_{2h} g) with total variation ≤ 0.26 P^{−5/16} over the block and is removed by one partial summation (Lemma 4.10) against the untwisted differenced sums on initial sub-intervals, whose bound is nondecreasing in the length; in the single-smooth-sum cases the twist’s curvature 0.13 P^{1/24−23/16} is dominated by powers of P. Corollary 4.13 (the OOEEE production on even blocks): for m′ ≥ 2 and I(m′) = [m′^{32/9}, (m′+1)^{32/9}), #{odd n ∈ I(m′) : word₅(n) = OOEEE, J⁵(n) = m′} = (1/16)#{odd n ∈ I(m′)} + O(|I(m′)| m′^{−4/27+ε}), via the nesting bound 0 ≤ n^{9/16} − v^{1/4} ≤ n^{−15/16}, an Erdős–Turán/Kusmin–Landau bound Y P^{−1/16} for the exceptional set, and a Vaaler expansion of the fifth letter whose modes are the slow twists. This discharges Hypothesis L of Paper C (Appendix C) to a Paper B theorem; Paper B remains a working draft. Not a halt theorem.

Paper B companion audit ledger docs/theory/paper_b_audit_ledger.md and research.juggler_sequence.paper_b_audit.
